title: `Metadata.from_email` hides validation errors when the input also has an unknown field
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging import metadata
metadata.Metadata.from_email(
    "Metadata-Version: 2.6\nName: packaging\n"
    "Unknown-Field: value\nVersion: invalid version\n")
```
Expected: one `ExceptionGroup` listing both problems, `unrecognized field: 'unknown-field'` and the invalid `version`.
Actual: `ExceptionGroup('unparsed', ...)` with only the unknown-field error; the bad version shows up only after that is fixed. Likewise `from_email("Hello: PyPA")` reports `hello` but not the missing `metadata-version`, `name` and `version`.

With validation on, `from_email` should report every problem at once: a single `ExceptionGroup` whose message is always `"invalid or unparsed metadata"`, holding an `InvalidMetadata` with the right `field` for each problem, and not chained to another exception (`__context__` is `None`). A required field given twice (e.g. two `Name:` lines) is reported once, as invalid data, not also as missing. Valid input still returns a `Metadata`.
acceptance: Unknown/unparsed fields and validation errors are reported together in one `invalid or unparsed metadata` group
A duplicated required field gives exactly one error for that field
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
